strongest_objection: The map's anchor observed case is stale in the tree by the map's own mechanism. Kept over before, the edge to Shared ledger, the near priority, the form inference, and the mode all state in the present tense that the climb's picker skips regate lines but not repair lines. In src/Ideonomy/Climb.hs the lastBreath filter skips both, landed as commit 809dd01 at 2026-09-13 15:33:23Z, forty-five seconds after the ledger's breath-two stamp. Every count the item gives (35 of 38 repair breaths at 1.00, 35 of 81 lists) matches the committed tree at the moment of writing, and four untracked fleet ledgers have already moved them to 39 of 42 and 85, so the record is a snapshot read as the live state, which is the map's own Pull, not push. This does not break the mechanism, which is real and verified: the repair breath's candidates equal its items-before by rule and the ratio cannot exceed one. It means the item must carry the commit it was observed at, the near priority's experiment must be run at that commit's parent, and the map should say that a map naming a defect in its own pipeline is repaired before it is admitted. The second real defect: Read back from disk's only observed case, the equals-sign separator, never touched disk; zsh took a word beginning with an equals sign as a command-path request. It is Answered a different question wearing the wrong handle. What I could not break: the item type holds for all seventeen, the neighbour pairs separate on a test a reader can run, and no item is a tip.

items.item: Empty return: the loop returns nothing and the reasoner supplies the reading, since a null from an environment that answered none and a null from a probe that never touched its target arrive as the same empty string; the carrier is any query whose null result is legal, a search that matched nothing, a listing of the wrong path, a poll of a queue, a question nobody answered; what the environment adds is nothing, which is the whole difficulty, since the reasoner cannot tell whether nothing was added or nothing was asked; the latency is the probe's and it can be re-asked freely, and the same probe returns the same nothing; the degenerate closure is reading the void as a finding, no members, no changes, no objection, consent, and the operator's rule that another agent's silence is never the user's consent exists because this closure is common; the tell is a return with no denominator, no count of what was searched and no evidence that the probe touched anything, and the changed move is to put the same probe to a case whose answer is known to be nonempty before believing its none; observed, including in this map's own making, where a search for a record by name returned nothing because the key on disk was written with a space the pattern lacked. Not enumeration-stalls' Never met one, where the enumerator's experience ran out, since here the environment was asked and the answer is void.
items.why: Distinct mechanism with carrier, latency, closure, and tell; the operator rule it cites (another agent's silence is not the user's consent) is a live rule in this session's own brief, so the doctrine is observed.

items.item: Read back from disk: the reasoner's output returns as the bytes actually on disk, read later by the same reasoner, and the environment adds the difference between what was meant and what was written, the truncation, the shell's expansion of a token the reasoner took as literal, the here-document that interpolated a dollar sign, the overwrite a concurrent writer made in between; the carrier is the file system; the latency is seconds and it can be re-asked freely with an identical answer until something writes; the degenerate closure is not re-reading, so the reasoner quotes its memory of the write as the state of the file and the read is of its own intent rather than of the disk; the tell is that the reasoner can cite the file's contents without having opened it since it wrote them; observed, as the line of five equals signs meant as a separator that the shell read as a command lookup and returned as not found. Not window-successions' file, which a stranger reads; here the writer reads it and the only loss is what the carrier changed on the way down and back.
items.why: Its only observed case is not an instance of its mechanism. The equals-sign separator was never written to disk; zsh took a word beginning with an equals sign as a request for a command's path and reported not found. That is the carrier's grammar rewriting the ask, which is Answered a different question. Replaced with a case in which bytes actually differ from intent on disk.
items.repair: Read back from disk: the reasoner's output returns as the bytes actually on disk, read later by the same reasoner, and the environment adds the difference between what was meant and what was written, the truncation, the shell's expansion of a token the reasoner took as literal, the here-document that interpolated a dollar sign, the overwrite a concurrent writer made in between; the carrier is the file system; the latency is seconds and it can be re-asked freely with an identical answer until something writes; the degenerate closure is not re-reading, so the reasoner quotes its memory of the write as the state of the file and the read is of its own intent rather than of the disk; the tell is that the reasoner can cite the file's contents without having opened it since it wrote them; observed, as the unquoted here-document whose body the shell expands before the bytes reach the file, so the read returns a variable's value where the reasoner wrote its name, and the file the reasoner remembers writing was never on disk. Not window-successions' file, which a stranger reads; here the writer reads it and the only loss is what the carrier changed on the way down and back.

items.item: Answered a different question: the carrier parses the ask under its own grammar before the environment answers, so the return is a true answer to a question the reasoner did not put; the carrier is a shell that expands, a pattern language in which a dot is any character, a comparison with a null that is never true, an index that stems the word, a form that cuts the field at forty characters; what the environment adds is correct and irrelevant; the latency and re-ask are the tool's, and re-asking in the same words reproduces the substitution exactly, which is the tell: the answer is stable, plausible, and does not vary with the part of the ask that mattered; the degenerate closure is reading that stability as the world's; the changed move is to put, through the same carrier, a question whose answer is already known and see whether it comes back; observed. Not Empty return, where nothing comes back, since here a full answer comes back to the wrong question, and the two meet only where the rewritten ask matches nothing.
items.why: Receives the equals-sign case from Read back from disk, where it belongs, so the observed modality is carried by a case a reader can reproduce in one line.
items.repair: Answered a different question: the carrier parses the ask under its own grammar before the environment answers, so the return is a true answer to a question the reasoner did not put; the carrier is a shell that expands, a pattern language in which a dot is any character, a comparison with a null that is never true, an index that stems the word, a form that cuts the field at forty characters; what the environment adds is correct and irrelevant; the latency and re-ask are the tool's, and re-asking in the same words reproduces the substitution exactly, which is the tell: the answer is stable, plausible, and does not vary with the part of the ask that mattered; the degenerate closure is reading that stability as the world's; the changed move is to put, through the same carrier, a question whose answer is already known and see whether it comes back; observed, as the line of equals signs meant as a separator that the shell took for a request for a command's path, since a word beginning with an equals sign is one under its grammar, and answered, correctly, that no such command exists. Not Empty return, where nothing comes back, since here a full answer comes back to the wrong question, and the two meet only where the rewritten ask matches nothing.

items.item: Green by construction: the reasoner writes both the artifact and the check that reads it, so the check returns the artifact's behaviour as its specification and passes on the day it is written by construction; the carrier is a test suite derived from the implementation, a golden file recorded from the current output, an acceptance criterion written after the work; what the environment adds is nothing today and persistence later, since the check will report when the behaviour changes, which is real information, so the loop is worth nothing on the first day and something on the ninetieth; the latency is seconds and it can be re-asked without limit; the degenerate closure is green read as correct; the tell is a check that has never been red and a failing case that nobody can name; the changed move is one case written from the requirement without looking at the code, run first; observed. Not Kept over before, where the verdict can still move and the denominator cannot; here the verdict itself was fixed when the check was derived.
items.why: Distinct: the verdict fixed at derivation time, and the ninety-day asymmetry is a real claim about what the loop adds and when.

items.item: Kept over before: a pass that may only cut reports a ratio whose denominator the rule fixed, so the number reads as a measurement and is a restatement of the rule; the carrier is the ledger line's keep rate, kept over candidates, where the repair breath's candidates are set equal to the items before it because it may not add; what the environment adds is at most the cuts, so the ratio is bounded at one and cannot rise, and in the observed ledgers 35 of the 38 repair breaths sit at 1.00 and three at 0.94 from a single cut each; the latency is zero and re-asking returns the same number; the degenerate closure lies downstream, since the climb's target picker reads each list's last keep rate as its gradient and skips the regate lines on the stated ground that survival is not growth yield, but not the repair lines, so 35 of 81 lists present a gradient of 1.00 that no growth measured and outrank every list whose last honest rate was 0.56 or 0.89; the tell is a returned number with almost no variance across cases, since a world would have scattered it; the changed move is the filter the picker already applies to one author, applied to the other; observed. Not Green by construction, where the verdict is fixed; here the verdict can move and only the ceiling is the rule's.
items.why: Its downstream closure, the picker that skipped regate lines but not repair lines, is asserted in the present tense and is false in the tree: src/Ideonomy/Climb.hs lastBreath skips both fable-regate and fable-repair as of commit 809dd01 (2026-09-13 15:33:23Z), 45 seconds after the ledger's breath-two stamp. The counts (35 of 38 at 1.00, 81 lists) match the committed tree at the time of writing; four untracked fleet ledgers already move them to 39 of 42 and 85. The mechanism survives; the case must carry its commit.
items.repair: Kept over before: a pass that may only cut reports a ratio whose denominator the rule fixed, so the number reads as a measurement and is a restatement of the rule; the carrier is the ledger line's keep rate, kept over candidates, where the repair breath's candidates are set equal to the items before it because it may not add; what the environment adds is at most the cuts, so the ratio is bounded at one and cannot rise, and in the ledgers as committed on 2026-09-13, 35 of the 38 repair breaths sat at 1.00 and three at 0.94 from a single cut each; the latency is zero and re-asking returns the same number; the degenerate closure lies downstream and was live in the climb's target picker until commit 809dd01, forty-five seconds after this map's second breath: the picker read each list's last keep rate as its gradient and skipped the regate lines on the stated ground that survival is not growth yield, but not the repair lines, so 35 of 81 lists presented a gradient of 1.00 that no growth measured and outranked every list whose last honest rate was 0.56 or 0.89; the tell is a returned number with almost no variance across cases, since a world would have scattered it; the changed move is the filter the picker applied to one author, applied to the other, which is the one string comparison that commit added; observed, and repaired within the hour, so the case is checkable only at that commit's parent. Not Green by construction, where the verdict is fixed; here the verdict can move and only the ceiling is the rule's.

items.item: Closed traverse: the reasoner walks a loop back to its own starting point and the environment returns the sum of its errors as the gap between where it stands and where it began; the carrier is the surveyor's traverse closing on the first station, the trial balance whose debits must meet its credits, the checksum, the quantity converted to another unit and back; what the environment adds is the one number the reasoner could not compute leg by leg, the accumulated error, with no indication of which leg carried it; the latency is the length of the loop and it can be re-asked by walking again; the degenerate closure is distributing the misclosure across the legs by rule and reporting the adjusted loop, which closes exactly by construction, so an exact closure reads as accuracy, and in the books the same closure is the compensating error, two mistakes that cancel and leave the balance sound; the tell is a closure that is exact rather than small; observed. Adds to Green by construction what a self-consistency check needs in order to carry information: two paths made independently, which the traverse's legs are and the test derived from the code is not.
items.why: Compass-rule adjustment and compensating errors are documented mechanisms; the checksum is a weaker fit (two computations compared, not a walk back to the start) but does not carry the item.

items.item: Leading question: the reasoner asks the user in a form that contains its own proposal, so the reply returns a signature on the reasoner's output and not the thing the user knew; the carrier is the yes-or-no question, the shall-I-proceed, the draft presented for approval; what the environment could have added, intent, is exactly what the form excluded, and what it adds instead is authority; the latency is hours and it can be re-asked at a cost that rises with each ask, since the asker spends the user's patience; the degenerate closure is the ok read as an instruction, and its formal twin is the rule that questions are not instructions, which exists because the closure is common; the tell is a reply shorter than the question; the changed move is to ask for what the user knows and the reasoner does not, the constraint, the preference, the fact, rather than for a signature; analytical, with the doctrine observed. Not Once, where the reader was chosen for having no stake; here the reader is the one whose stake the reasoner needed and the form threw it away.
items.why: Analytical, marked so, with the rule that questions are not instructions observed in the operator's global context. The tell is thin but real.

items.item: Laundered echo: the reasoner's output leaves through one channel and returns through another with its origin stripped, so it reads as independent corroboration; the carrier is a claim placed in an encyclopedia, printed by a newspaper that read it there, and then cited by the encyclopedia to the newspaper; one defector's report reaching an analyst through three liaison services as three reports; a summary an agent wrote, quoted by a colleague, read back by the agent as the colleague's finding; a fleet's maps read by the next fleet's author as the shape of the subject rather than the shape of the fleet; what the environment adds is a second signature and a delay, and what it strips is the first signature; the latency is days to years and each re-ask multiplies the copies; the degenerate closure is the mechanism itself; the tell is that the corroborating source's wording matches the reasoner's own, and that the count of independent sources falls to one when traced; observed in circular reporting and in citation loops, and speculative for the fleet case, which this map cannot measure from inside. Not enumeration-stalls' Two nets, one boat, where two enumerators miss the same members for the same reason; here one enumerator's members return as a second enumerator's.
items.why: Citation loops and the defector-through-three-services case are documented; the fleet case is marked speculative and the map says it cannot measure it from inside. Correct modality discipline.

items.item: Own footprint: the reasoner's act moves the quantity it reads, so the return is the world plus the reasoner's own pressure, inseparably; the carrier is the price after the order, the poll after the campaign, the metric after the announcement, the queue after the poll of it; what the environment adds is everyone else's acts, mixed with the reasoner's in a proportion it does not know; the latency runs from milliseconds to days and it can be re-asked, but every ask is an act that moves it again; the degenerate closure is reading the move the reasoner caused as information about what it was measuring, the momentum that was its own order, the interest that was its own broadcast; the tell is that the move reverses when the reasoner stops; observed, as the temporary and permanent components of market impact. Not Laundered echo, where the reasoner's output comes back under someone else's signature; here it comes back under none.
items.why: The tell as written, the move reverses when the reasoner stops, is contradicted by the item's own cited literature: only the temporary component reverses; the permanent component of market impact does not. The repaired tell keeps the mechanism and says which part reverses.
items.repair: Own footprint: the reasoner's act moves the quantity it reads, so the return is the world plus the reasoner's own pressure, inseparably; the carrier is the price after the order, the poll after the campaign, the metric after the announcement, the queue after the poll of it; what the environment adds is everyone else's acts, mixed with the reasoner's in a proportion it does not know; the latency runs from milliseconds to days and it can be re-asked, but every ask is an act that moves it again; the degenerate closure is reading the move the reasoner caused as information about what it was measuring, the momentum that was its own order, the interest that was its own broadcast; the tell is the part of the move that reverses when the reasoner stops, which was the reasoner's own, while the part that stays is the world's or the information the act leaked, and the two cannot be told apart until the reasoner stops; observed, as the temporary and permanent components of market impact. Not Laundered echo, where the reasoner's output comes back under someone else's signature; here it comes back under none.

items.item: Shared ledger: the environment returns a record to which others also write, and the reasoner counts their lines as its own because the record does not say whose they are; the carrier is an append-only log with a shared name, a metric that several processes increment, a queue several workers drain; what the environment adds is others' output, unlabelled; the latency is zero and it can be re-asked; the degenerate closure is the reasoner reading others' work as its own spend, its own progress, or its own history, and the observed case is the climb's spend level, a decayed sum over the timestamps of every line in its ledger directory, where 76 fieldwork lines and 38 repair lines written by the fieldwork and repair passes sit beside the machine's own and each counts as a breath the machine took; the tell is a rate of one's own activity that moves when one is idle; the changed move is a by-field read before the line is counted; observed by reading the code, not by watching it stall. The mirror of Laundered echo, where one's own output returns as others'; here others' returns as one's own, and a reasoner in both loops at once cannot tell which way it is being fooled.
items.why: Verified against src/Ideonomy/Climb.hs ledgerLevel, which sums exp(-age/tau) over every line of every file in the ledger directory with no read of the by-field; the header comment calls this the climb ledger's own timestamps, so the mis-attribution is real. Counts (76 fieldwork, 38 repair) matched the committed tree at writing; today's tree holds 84 and 42. Keep, with the item's own caveat that it is read from code and not watched.

items.item: Lagged gauge: the return arrives after the reasoner has already acted again, so it reads a state it has since changed and corrects a correction; the carrier is a dashboard that aggregates on a delay, a stock report a month behind the orders, the pipe between a shower's tap and its head; what the environment adds is the true state at a past instant; the latency is the mechanism, and it can be re-asked, always late by the same amount; the degenerate closure is chasing one's own previous correction, so that an oscillation with a period near twice the lag is read as the world's volatility; the tell is the period; observed, as the bullwhip in a supply chain and the overshoot of any controller fed a delayed measurement. Not Clock, since the clock is what makes the lag a number; without a clock read beside the gauge the lag is invisible and the oscillation has no cause.
items.why: Keep. The period claim, near twice the lag, holds for relay control with pure delay; for proportional control it runs two to four times the delay. Noted under modality, not worth a repair.

items.item: Compiler's list: the reasoner's whole text returns as a list of its consequences under rules the reasoner holds only in part, at once and in seconds; the carrier is a compiler, a type checker, a linter, a proof assistant, a schema validator; what the environment adds is consequence at a distance, the change on line three that fails line four hundred, under rules the reasoner had not internalized and could not have run in its head over the whole; the latency is seconds, it can be re-asked without limit, and it is deterministic, so re-asking with nothing changed is pure echo; the degenerate closure is editing to the error's text rather than to its cause, the cast that silences the type error, the annotation that satisfies the checker, the suppression comment, so that the next return is the reasoner's own decision and compiles is read as correct; the tell is a fix that changed the annotation and not the value; observed. Adds to denominator-manufactures' Compiler's catalogue, which takes the error list as a universe to count against, the loop's question: whether the list still comes from the rules or from the reasoner's edit of what the rules are shown.
items.why: Distinct from Green by construction by the fork edge; the cast and suppression comment are the right carriers for the closure.

items.item: Ping: the reasoner emits solely to get a return, and the environment adds range and shape by what it does to the emission; the carrier is sonar, radar, a health-check request, a canary release, an order for one share, a trial balloon; what the environment adds is time of flight, attenuation, and what bounced, none of which the reasoner could know before emitting; the latency is the distance and it can be re-asked at will; the degenerate closure is reverberation, reading the multipath echoes of one's own ping as targets and the wall one is standing beside as an object in the field; the tell is a target that moves when the reasoner moves; observed. Not Own footprint, where the act was for its own sake and moved the world; here the act is the question, and the reasoner would not have emitted if it did not want the answer.
items.why: The tell, a target that moves when the reasoner moves, does not separate reverberation from a real target, since every range changes when the emitter moves. The sonar tell is the opposite: a return whose range stays fixed as the emitter moves, or that sits at a multiple of a known reflector's range.
items.repair: Ping: the reasoner emits solely to get a return, and the environment adds range and shape by what it does to the emission; the carrier is sonar, radar, a health-check request, a canary release, an order for one share, a trial balloon; what the environment adds is time of flight, attenuation, and what bounced, none of which the reasoner could know before emitting; the latency is the distance and it can be re-asked at will; the degenerate closure is reverberation, reading the multipath echoes of one's own ping as targets and the wall one is standing beside as an object in the field; the tell is a return whose range does not change as the reasoner moves, the hull, the wall it carries with it, or one that sits at a whole multiple of a known reflector's range; observed. Not Own footprint, where the act was for its own sake and moved the world; here the act is the question, and the reasoner would not have emitted if it did not want the answer.

items.item: Pull, not push: the environment changes without telling the reasoner and returns its state only when asked, so the reasoner is late by exactly as long as it went without asking; the carrier is a repository others push to, a shared file, a database, a mailbox with no notification; what the environment adds is what others did since the last ask; the latency is unbounded until the ask and seconds after it, and it can be re-asked freely; the degenerate closure is reading the last snapshot as the live state, the tree's status taken at the start of a session read as the tree now; the tell is that the answer the reasoner holds is older than its own last act on the thing; observed. Not Lagged gauge, where the environment is late; here the environment is current and the reasoner is late, so the cure is not a faster gauge but a habit of asking before acting.
items.why: Distinct from Lagged gauge by whose lateness it is; the tell (the held answer is older than one's own last act on the thing) is readable from the reasoner's side. This map's own record is an instance: see strongest_objection.

items.item: Clock: the loop that always answers and never the same, in which the reasoner's act is stamped and the return is the elapsed time since, which no record of the reasoner's own can hold, since a reasoner does not feel its own duration; the carrier is the wall clock and the timestamps on the ledger; what the environment adds is elapsed time and the true order of events, which memory reorders; the latency is zero and it can be re-asked without limit, each answer different; the degenerate closure is computing now from one's own last stamp, so that the clock is read against the record instead of the record against the clock, and a paused reasoner resumes believing no time has passed; the tell is a clock that agrees with the record exactly; observed, as the session resumed after an hour that acts on a state it last saw before the hour. Not Pull, not push, where what changed is others' acts; here nothing may have changed but the time, and the time is enough to make the last read stale.
items.why: Distinct: the only return that always differs and holds nothing of the reasoner; the resumed-session case is observed operator doctrine.

items.item: Once: a reader with no memory of the reasoner's reasoning returns a verdict on the text alone, and the ask spends the freshness, so the same question cannot be put again, since the second reader has seen the first verdict or the first reader is no longer fresh; the carrier is the fresh-context critic, the specimen consumed by a destructive test, the first user who will never again not know the product; what the environment adds is what the text says without what the author meant; the latency is minutes to hours; the degenerate closure has two forms, the seat's menu returning its attractor, as the 38 critiques across three fleets that all returned admit-with-repairs, which the author read as the map's grade, and the correction of that, a brief that tells the critic the fact so that the critic now avoids the attractor because told, which is a second echo wearing the first's cure; the tell of spent freshness is a verdict that cites the previous verdict; observed. Not Blinded return, where the reader is stripped of the author's expectation by design and can be re-run on a new arm; here the reader is stripped by never having had it, and there is no new arm.
items.why: Distinct from Blinded return by re-runnability. Its second closure, the brief that tells the critic about the attractor, is this critique's own situation; the tell it names (a verdict that cites the previous verdict) is one this critique has tried to avoid by checking the repo rather than the seat.

items.item: Blinded return: the loop is built so that the return cannot carry the reasoner's expectation, since the reasoner is removed from the part of the environment that decides; the carrier is the double-blind trial, the judge who sees candidates without their proposer, the seriation whose order is measured by one process while its axis is named by another, the review with the author's name cut off; what the environment adds is the outcome independent of hope; what it costs is that the return cannot carry intent either, so a blinded judge can say whether the text holds and not whether the target was preserved; the latency is the trial's, months, and it cannot be re-asked on the same arm, since once the blind is broken the loop is closed for that specimen; the degenerate closure is unblinding by tell, the side effect that reveals the arm, the voice that reveals the author, so that the return quietly carries the expectation again; the tell is a blinded read that agrees with the unblinded one on cases where the arm was guessable; observed. Not Once, where the reader was never given the author's reasoning; here the reader may have everything but the one thing, and the mechanism is the subtraction, which can be repeated on a new arm.
items.why: Distinct; the cost claim (a blinded judge cannot rule on the target) is the load-bearing inference for the last edge and holds.

neighbor_test.left: Lagged gauge: the return arrives after the reasoner has already acted again, so it reads a state it has since changed and corrects a correction.
neighbor_test.right: Pull, not push: the environment changes without telling the reasoner and returns its state only when asked, so the reasoner is late by exactly as long as it went without asking.
neighbor_test.separating_case: A reasoner reads a git tree's status at the start of a session and acts on it an hour later; the same reasoner reads a CI dashboard that aggregates on a ten-minute delay. Ask both again now. The tree answers with the present, so the earlier staleness was the reasoner's, Pull, not push; the dashboard answers with ten minutes ago, so the staleness is the carrier's, Lagged gauge. The test is one re-ask, and the two items give opposite cures: a habit for the first, and for the second no habit helps, only a smaller hand or a longer wait. The pair does not collapse. This map's own record is the first case: it read the picker before commit 809dd01 and did not ask again.

boundary_case: A counter the reasoner increments itself and reads back, a progress bar computed from its own count of steps: tempting, because it is read as if it were the clock, and it is out, since nothing outside the reasoner adds anything and the reading is memory. The moment the bar is computed against wall-clock stamps it is in as Clock, and the moment it is computed against a shared metric that other processes increment it is in as Shared ledger. The ruling sharpens Clock's fence: the return is elapsed time only when the environment, not the reasoner, supplied the stamp.

seriation.note: The itinerary holds as an authored walk and should not be reordered. Its hinge at Lagged gauge, the first return that is the world and not the reasoner, is defensible, and the two runs (the self-consistency trio; the mixture quartet from self-as-other to other-as-self) teach by adjacency. One correction to the note: the form inference calls Lagged gauge and Own footprint a loop, but the graph holds one directed edge between them and no cycle; the loop is in the world (act, gauge, act) and the note should say so rather than claim the map draws it. With Kept over before repaired to past tense the note's clause 'the edge from the traverse to the ratio says how the one becomes the other' should read against the repaired label, which now passes by the shared tell of missing spread rather than by exact closure.

edges.why: A real conditional whose antecedent fails when the rewritten ask still matches something, and the label says what happens then; it also correctly limits the known-positive probe to the empty case.

The fork is genuine: the same red-to-green diff lands on either side depending on whether it touched the value or the annotation, and the antecedent (the edit changed what the checker is shown) can fail. The colon tell is narrow to typed languages but is a tell, not a rule.

The consequent contradicts the map's own neighbour test. An adjusted traverse that closes exactly by rule is a verdict that cannot move, which the separating case assigns to Green by construction; Kept over before is the number that can still move down. The passage that actually holds between the two is the shared tell: a rule applied before reporting removes the spread the world would have supplied.
edges.repair_label: If the misclosure is distributed across the legs by rule before the loop is reported, the reported closure carries no spread across surveys, exactly as the repair breath's rate carries almost none across maps, so a reader who sees many closures at exactly zero, or many rates at exactly one, is reading the rule and not the survey; where the raw misclosure or the cut count is reported beside the rule's number, the spread returns and the check keeps its information, and where only the rule's number is reported the traverse has become Kept over before with a survey for a carrier, a number that could have moved and did not.

edges.why: The label asserts in the present tense that the picker cannot see the rule and ranks 35 repaired lists first; commit 809dd01 at 15:33:23Z added the fable-repair string to the same filter as fable-regate, 45 seconds after this map's second breath. The passage between levels is real and generic; the repo case must be dated.
edges.repair_label: If a number fixed by one pass's rule is written into a ledger that a second loop reads as its own measurement, the rule crosses a level and becomes the second loop's world; the climb's picker did this until commit 809dd01 on 2026-09-13, ranking 35 repaired lists above every list whose last rate was measured because it read the by-field for regate lines and not for repair lines; a by-field read before the number is counted breaks the passage, and that break cost one string comparison, which is the whole of that commit.

edges.why: A real conditional with a failing antecedent (a reader given items and the of-sentence alone). It describes this fleet's own critic seat, which hands the critic the ledger with the author's gaps and the gate's self-read; the tell it names is checkable on every critique file in the directory.

The claim that the cure is not a faster gauge is false as stated: shortening the lag shortens the period and lowers the overshoot for any gain. The condition that the loop closes only where the reasoner's acts are large against the world's is the real content and should stand alone.
edges.repair_label: If the gauge lags and the reasoner's own acts are a large part of what it gauges, the return is the reasoner's previous act arriving late, so each correction reads as a fresh move of the world and the reasoner chases itself with a period set by the lag; where the reasoner's acts are small against the world's, the lag is only a delay and the loop between the two does not close, so a faster gauge shortens the chase but only a smaller hand or a longer wait opens the loop.
